excluded_families.reason: pose and alignment controls, not structural neck shortening
surface shape controls such as front curve, double chin, and Adams apple
sex- and archetype-specific macro components that would change body identity
archetype-specific upper-trunk shape, not a universal length control

observations: The three affected source bodyfits have no nonzero junction morphs before face assembly.
The three affected composed characters also have no nonzero junction morphs after face assembly.
The long-neck appearance is therefore inherited from the selected Body Shape and Body Ratio macros.
The runtime catalog exposes Neck Length only in the non-negative range 0.0 to 1.0, so its shortening direction must be proven visually before production use.
The F01 endpoint test verified that embedded Neck Length 0.0 to 1.0 lengthens the neck and cannot satisfy the shortening requirement.
The composed F01 runtime reports Headshot Neck Height bounds of -1.0 to 0.5, which supersede the older combined-catalog bounds for this diagnostic.
The F01 focus test verified that Headshot Neck Height -1.0 to 0.0 shortens the neck monotonically; each -0.2 step lowers total avatar height by approximately 0.62 cm.
The F01 focus test restored all controlled Morphs, all protected Morphs, avatar yaw, and the original scene exactly.
Headshot contains overlapping neck controls and must not be mixed with the embedded Actor neck controls without an explicit policy.

recommended_strategy.calibration_policy: one fixed Neck Height value per affected bodyfit; never randomize this correction
recommended_strategy.fallback_policy: Only test shoulder height controls if Neck Height cannot produce a natural shoulder-to-neck transition.
recommended_strategy.headshot_overlap_policy: Do not combine this control with other Headshot neck Morphs unless a separate paired calibration is validated.
